name: CSharp FlashCards 2026
oneLiner: A deck of 269 Q&A flashcards on C# and .NET built as a Beamer deck on a 1080x1920 pt page, compiled to PDF by GitHub Actions on a `v*` tag.
summary: Every question gets its own slide, the answer is the next slide, and the whole lot sits in 24 `areas/*.tex` files pulled in by 24 `\input` directives from `main.tex`. The presentation layer is carried by a bespoke class `mybeamer.cls` (24 section colours, shared `minted` and `listings` configuration, an automatic Outline frame at the start of a section) plus `mybeamer.sty` with the macros `\QuestionSlide`, `\CategoryBadge` and `\TOCButtonTall`. The most interesting decision is in the geometry and it is unfinished: `main.tex` passes `paperwidth=1080pt` and `paperheight=1920pt` to the `geometry` package — phone-screen proportions — and the line below passes the `landscape` option to that same package, which swaps those dimensions round to 1920x1080. The repository holds neither a built PDF nor a LaTeX toolchain, so the final orientation cannot be confirmed from here — the source declares both at once. The second decision is already a failure, and you can see it in the code: `\AnswerSlide` is defined and **never used once**, because 197 `minted` blocks force `frame[fragile]`, so all 269 answers were written by hand instead of through the macro. Delivery is {{term:tagdeploy|release on a tag}} — `xelatex` with `-shell-escape` in the `xu-cheng/latex-action@v4` action, publishing `CSharp_FlashCards.pdf` as a GitHub Release. The content and the pipeline are finished; the wrapping — landing page, title slide, footer links — comes from the previous edition and nobody has updated it.
license: MIT-0 w pliku LICENSE, MIT na odznakach — rozjazd
tests: No tests. There is no test framework and no verification script; the only check is the fact that the LaTeX compile in CI has to succeed, and that fires only on a tag.
ci: Two workflows. `ci.yml` starts **only on a push of a `v*` tag**: it builds `main.tex` through `xu-cheng/latex-action@v4` with XeLaTeX and `shell_escape`, uploads the artefact and publishes a release through `softprops/action-gh-release@v2`. `pages.yml` deploys the `docs` directory to GitHub Pages on a change under `docs/**` or manually; neither workflow builds on an ordinary push or on a PR.

metrics.label: Questions with a difficulty prefix
metrics.value: 262 of 269 (55 x *, 173 x **, 34 x ***) — counted by parsing the mandatory argument of every \QuestionSlide with brace matching, including where the title sits on the line after the optional argument

docs.label: Generic prompt for the LaTeX repo generator

components.name: mybeamer.sty
components.description: A `qcounter` counter, a category badge drawn with TikZ, a fixed-height TOC tile and the slide macros. It contains not one string tied to C# or to this repository, so it moves verbatim into another deck — `MASTER_PROMPT.md` says so itself.

components.name: MASTER_PROMPT.md
components.description: 14 KB of specification for an LLM: how to generate a complete LaTeX repo from raw content — YAML metadata, a branch into book/article/flashcards/slides, a manifest of files in order, a Markdown-to-LaTeX mapping table and eight self-check points. Placeholders `{github_user}`, `{repo_name}`, `{pdf_name}` and an explicit ban on the subject matter leaking into the structural files.

components.name: Workflow buildu i wydania
components.description: Two jobs: build compiles with XeLaTeX and saves the artefact, release downloads it and publishes. Apart from the PDF file name there is nothing about C# here, so it is a ready-made {{term:tagdeploy|release-on-a-tag pipeline}} for any repository holding a TeX document.

components.name: Motyw Beamer deepdiveinto
components.description: 271 lines: a right-hand sidebar with a stack of steps, the `mbPrimary`/`mbAccent`/`mbSecondary` palette, `newunicodechar` mappings. Neutral on subject matter, but it drags along the macros `\coords`, `\mom`, `\pphi` from general relativity — cut those out before reusing it.

components.name: Subject-area files
components.description: From `1-csharp-language-beginner.tex` to `24-tooling-agile.tex`. The distribution is heavily uneven: C# Intermediate has 52 questions, Threading/Async 23, OAuth 21, and most of the remaining areas between 4 and 9.

components.name: mybeamer.cls
components.description: The class does not set the page size — it only does `\RequirePackage{geometry}`, and the dimensions and the `landscape` option arrive from `main.tex`. It holds 22 category colours plus `sec1bg`–`sec24bg`, a shared `CodeBg` background for `minted` and `listings`, and bespoke navigation symbols with a Contents button. The number of section colours is hard-wired to this deck's 24 areas, and the footer links to the old repository name.

components.name: main.tex
components.description: A title slide, an About slide and a contents grid of 24 clickable tiles leading to each section's `\hypertarget`. It pulls in the 24 area files; the title still reads 'C# Flashcards 2025 edition'.

components.name: Landing page
components.description: One file, 30,481 bytes, its own CSS tokens, light and dark mode, sample Q&A cards and quick-start tabs switched by a `switchTab` of a few lines. Zero external dependencies and zero figures that match the current state of the repo.

overlaps.reason: The same workshop: a long LaTeX document with its own preamble and class, built with `latexmk` and watched by CI. The conventions from one repo carry over to the other without translation.
Also a technical book in LaTeX addressed to .NET engineers, so the C#, Azure and patterns areas overlap in content in part.
`presentations/theme/beamerthemedeepdiveinto.sty` carries macros from general relativity, so the theme is either shared with or copied from the black-hole deck.
`docs/index.html` is the same class of artefact: a single-file static landing page published through GitHub Pages.
The deck is signed with the dev_insight brand, so it works as a distribution channel for the same identity.

product: No buyer. This is study material and interview preparation, given away free as a PDF under the {{term:mit|MIT-0 licence}}, so its function is channel and reputation: it builds recognition for the dev_insight brand and pulls traffic to GitHub. The real audience is a .NET developer ahead of an interview, or someone running a training course. Nobody will pay for the present form, because there is no spaced repetition here, no progress tracking and no interactive version — there is one static PDF, and that is the whole product.
highlights: 269 `\QuestionSlide` calls across `areas/*.tex` and 270 answer `frame`s — the mapping is one to one apart from a single question in `8-design-patterns.tex`, which has two answer frames. Nothing checks this automatically.
197 C# code blocks typeset by `minted` with one configuration (`linenos`, `CodeBg` background, `breakanywhere`) defined once in the class rather than per slide.

`MASTER_PROMPT.md` pulls a **LaTeX repository generator** out of this repo: a manifest of files in order, a branch into four document types and a self-check list. A repo that described itself as a template.
The delivery path has no manual step: a `v*` tag runs XeLaTeX in Actions and pushes `CSharp_FlashCards.pdf` to Releases.
gaps: **The landing page lies about the numbers.** `docs/index.html` claims a '300+ card Q&A deck' and 13 areas; there are 269 cards and 24 areas. This is a publicly visible page, so the {{term:drift|drift}} undermines the credibility of everything else written on it.
The year has drifted apart: the README says 2026, the title slide in `main.tex` and the landing page title still say 2025, and the `Copyright` in LICENSE is dated 2025 too.

`main.tex` and `mybeamer.cls` link to `konradcinkusz/CSharp-FlashCards-2025`, that is, **not to this repository**. The footer of each of several hundred PDF slides points at a name that does not exist.

The `\AnswerSlide` macro is defined and used **zero times** — `minted` forces `frame[fragile]`, so all 269 answers go round the API and write the frame by hand. Dead code plus a mismatch between the declared interface and the practice.

262 of 269 questions carry a `*`, `**` or `***` prefix (55 / 173 / 34); 7 have none, and 6 of those are consecutive steps of a single OAuth flow. The asterisks render literally in the slide title and there is no legend anywhere, so the reader sees noise instead of a difficulty scale.

`main.tex` declares the orientation twice and contradicts itself: lines 1–3 pass `paperwidth=1080pt`/`paperheight=1920pt` to `geometry`, and line 4 passes `landscape`, which swaps the dimensions to 1920x1080. Without a built PDF there is no settling which declaration wins.

Links to `releases/latest` have been removed from the live section: `git tag` returns not one tag, `ci.yml` fires only on a push of a `v*` tag, and there is no built PDF in the repository — from the repository alone there is no confirming that any release was ever produced.
risks: Licence mismatch: LICENSE is MIT No Attribution, while the badge in the README and on the landing page says MIT. Two different agreements in one repository.
CI builds only on a `v*` tag, and locally there is no tag at all — the repository gives no way to confirm whether any release was actually produced, or whether `main` compiles at all.

Name collision: the repository is `csharp-flashcards`, but the code inside links consistently to `CSharp-FlashCards-2025`, and the landing page footer leads to an entirely different project (AgentHelm).
`presentations/` is wired into no build and into no `main.tex`, and the theme drags in macros from another field. At the next edition this will be the first thing to mislead.
next: Count the cards with a script and put the true 269 and 24 areas into the README, the landing page and the About slide. An inflated number on a public page costs more than everything else on this list.

Replace every reference to `CSharp-FlashCards-2025` in `main.tex` and `mybeamer.cls` with `konradcinkusz/csharp-flashcards` and settle the year at 2026 on the title slide and in the landing page title.
Add a job to `ci.yml` that compiles `main.tex` on a push to `main` and on a pull request, so broken LaTeX is caught before tagging rather than at release.
Settle `\AnswerSlide`: either delete the dead macro, or rework it into a `fragile` variant that handles `minted` and rewrite the 269 frames onto it.
Align LICENSE with the badge — one or the other, MIT-0 or MIT — and fix the year on the copyright line.
headline: Content finished; the landing says 300+ cards and 13 areas, it is 269 and 24
